function.name: law_case_get_details
function.description: Fetches detailed information on a specific case including its history and the litigants involved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

case_number.description: The unique number identifying the case.

include_history.description: Flag indicating if case history should be included. Default is false.

include_litigants.description: Flag indicating if litigant details should be included. Default is false.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find case details for case numbers 28473 and 64725, including litigant details and history. We need to call the function law_case_get_details twice, once for each case number. The function signature: law_case_get_details takes case_number (string), include_history? default false, include_litigants? default false. But we want both history and litigants. So set include_history=true, include_litigants=true.

We need to produce calls to the function. According to guidelines, we should output a single function call with arguments. But we have two cases. We can either call twice or combine? The function only accepts one case_number. So we need to call twice. The guidelines say "When calling a function, you must provide a single function call with arguments." That means we cannot embed multiple calls in a single JSON. But we can produce two separate function calls sequentially. The system will handle them. So we produce first call for case 28473, then second call for case 64725. Each call is separate. We'll do it in order.
